title: V. The good suited to the rational immortal soul; proof that man has a rational soul
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss: concerning its nature the following rules stand as to be observed here in passing. that same which from so excellent an effect we call rational; — this stands as the soul. From that same which we gather that same there stands as in us some principle from that same which this operation flows. that same which stands as to reason — for we understand that same we arrive from known things at knowledge belonging toward unknowns. plus we all experience it from the operations belonging toward the soul in us — this stands as confessed among all. Man has a rational soul: but if he falls from it he will be extremely wretched. when he has obtained it he will be happy plus blessed; that same which stands as immaterial, indissoluble, plus immortal, such a good suits him as exceeds the measure plus duration belonging toward the body plus endures with the immortal soul itself after departure from the body: — since therefore man stands as endowed with a rational soul. V.
pass_b_english: V. Since therefore man is endowed with a rational soul, which is immaterial, indissoluble, and immortal, such a good suits him as exceeds the measure and duration of the body and endures with the immortal soul itself after departure from the body: when he has obtained it he will be happy and blessed; but if he falls from it he will be extremely wretched.

Man has a rational soul: this is confessed among all, and we all experience it from the operations of the soul in us. For we understand that we arrive from known things at knowledge of unknowns, which is to reason.

From which we gather that there is in us some principle from which this operation flows. This is the soul, which from so excellent an effect we call rational; concerning its nature the following rules are to be observed here in passing.
source_text: V. Cum itaque homo praeditus sit anima rationali, quae immateriata, indissolubilis & immortalis est, ejusmodi bonum ei convenit, quod mensuram & durationem corporis excedat, & cum ipsa anima immortali post discessum a corpore perennet: quo potita fuerit, felix & beata; sin vero exciderit, extreme misera erit. HOMINI anima rationalis est: id quod tum apud omnes in confesso est, tum ex operationibus animae in nobis omnes experimur. Nam intelligimus, nos e notis in ignotorum notitiam pervenire, quod est ratiocinari. Ex quo colligimus, esse in nobis principium aliquod, a quo operatio isthaec fluat. Hoc vero est anima, quam a tam excellenti effectu rationalem appellamus, de cujus natura hic obiter sequentes regulae observandae sunt.
